correctness.rationale: Any sufficiently large positive common multiple of cycle lengths gives the same idempotent for a map; a positive power shares it. Thus no edge crosses its classes, and every class is connected via the idempotent. For a fixed idempotent e a map with eventual power e commutes with e, permutes its roots by σ, sends each fiber i into fiber σ(i), and has no nonroot cycle. Conversely those conditions send every point to a root, which must be the root of its original fiber at any sufficiently large multiple of the root permutation order. For a fixed σ, sum each row of the forest matrix over choices of its outgoing arrow x→y: use the row unit vector at x minus that at y for a nonroot target, and just the row unit vector at x for a root. An assignment with a nonroot cycle gives a row dependence, including a zero row for a loop; an acyclic assignment gives determinant one by ordering vertices by distance to roots. Factoring the resulting L=D−PQ reduces to I−QD⁻¹P, with the sole possible entry in row i at σ(i) equal to b_{σ(i)}/m_{σ²(i)}. Thus per cycle the reduced factor is 1−∏ b_i/m_i, including singleton cycles. Empty nonroot set gives one per permutation; the rank-one factor gives n^{n−2} at n≥2 and one at n=1. At n=5 the two rank-two contributions are 16+1 and 3+8, with 20 and 60 root/fiber assignments. The only unequal profiles at equal rank for n<5 are (3,1) and (2,2) at rank two for n=4; both give size 4. Independent replay /workspace/branches/review_replay_2.py checked through n=5 using first-repeat orbit phases, not the supplied common-exponent code; it confirms the first split and multiplicities, not the all-n theorem.
